## About

Robbie Torres is a Technical Program Manager based in Oakland, California. He has over 12 years of experience in e-commerce platform operations, web development, people management, and data analytics. He has managed web operations for 30+ websites, led a $20M e-commerce platform migration, built and led a frontend engineering team, and shipped production applications on Cloudflare Workers. He uses Claude daily as a working partner for code generation, debugging, data analysis, SQL, SOPs, and stakeholder communications.

His scope has consistently spanned four areas that are often separate roles: platform development, e-commerce operations, people management, and analytics/reporting.

## Experience

### Manager of Web Systems & Development — Adair Family Wines (2024–2026)

Led web technology, e-commerce platforms, data analytics, and digital infrastructure across 6 properties. Built a custom Digital Asset Management platform on Cloudflare Workers, replacing $30K+/year commercial solutions at roughly $600/year. Built a multi-property health dashboard surfacing 1,800+ issues. One of 4 leads on a $20M platform migration and built the only internal tracking system for it. Built Black Friday/Cyber Monday infrastructure supporting $245K+ in sales across 750+ orders. Built unified GA4 and Looker Studio dashboards, identifying $436K in transactions with no prior visibility across 13 partners. Managed 4+ external vendors as primary technical escalation contact.

### Director of Web Dev & Programming — Vintage Wine Estates (2022–2024)

Directed technical operations across 30+ production e-commerce websites with a team of 2 frontend developers, owning hiring, performance management, and career development. Reduced page load times by up to 80%. Contributed to over 100% annual revenue growth for five consecutive years through strategic platform improvements, in partnership with the CTO and marketing leadership. Promoted a direct report from Web Developer to Senior Frontend Developer. Led the technical wind-down and migration following the company's Chapter 11 proceedings. Led Salsify PIM onboarding and MikMak analytics rollout.

### Senior Web Developer — Vintage Wine Estates (2018–2022)

First management role at the company: built and led the frontend engineering team while continuing hands-on development across 20+ brand sites. Built a custom wine club checkout workflow on CORESense with co-written APIs, achieving a 300% year-over-year revenue increase within 24 hours of launch. Led Talkable referral program integration and launched a native loyalty program. Ran A/B testing and CRO programs using Optimizely, VWO, Google Optimize, and Lucky Orange. Wrote MySQL queries for ad-hoc reporting supporting wine club operations, marketing, and platform migrations.

### Web Content Manager — Vintage Wine Estates (2013–2018)

Established Asana as the project management tool company-wide. Onboarded and migrated 25+ newly acquired brand websites, integrating responsive design and SEO best practices. Built a QR code generator used company-wide as a marketing tool.

### Web Producer — Spirit Clips, Hallmark Labs (2012–2013)

Helped launch Zendesk for customer service. Managed content operations for a digital film library platform with 700+ assets. Collaborated with technology partners and assisted the CTO with SOPs.

## Case study: replacing a $30K DAM with $600 of Cloudflare

Full writeup: https://robbietorres.info/work/dam-platform/

Seven winery brands needed one place for trade partners (distributors, retailers, on-premise accounts) to download labels, bottle shots, and tech sheets. Commercial digital asset management platforms quoted above $30,000 per year. Robbie built a custom platform on Cloudflare Workers instead, running at roughly $600 per year.

Architecture: Cloudflare Workers for application logic, routing, auth, and signed download URLs; R2 for asset storage (no egress fees, which is the decisive cost factor for a download-heavy product); D1 for asset metadata, brand configuration, users, and the download log; KV for session and configuration caching; Pages for the per-brand front ends and internal admin.

Results: 5,852 downloads by 381 unique users, one branded portal per brand, and download analytics that answered questions the previous email-and-shared-drive process could not — which brands and SKUs partners actually request, which accounts are active, and which assets are unused. The reporting was not in the original brief and became the most-requested feature. The pattern was later productised as Trade Pourtal (https://tradepourtal.com).
